chunks: He said: Abul Hasan Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Katib informed me, he said: Abu Ali Muhammad ibn Hammam al-Iskafi narrated to us, he said: Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Tirmidhi narrated to me, he said: Ubaidullah ibn Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us, he said: Ja'far ibn Sulaiman al-Dhuba'i narrated to us, he said: I heard Malik ibn Dinar saying:

I came to the graveyard and stood over it, then I said: I came to the graves and called out to them: Where is the honored one and the despised? And where is he who answered when called, and where is the mighty one when he boasted? And where is the one conceited about his authority, and where is the powerful one when he wielded his power?

He said: Then a voice answered me from the direction of the graves, though I could see no form for it: They all perished together, and there is no trace left; they all died, and the news about them died too. The insects of the earth come and go, erasing the beauty of those faces. O you who ask me about people who have passed away, is there no lesson for you in what you see?
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad and his immaculate progeny, and grant them abundant peace.

key_terms.الجبانة: A deserted graveyard or open cemetery outside a town
key_terms.بنات الثرى: Daughters of the soil — a metaphor for earthworms and insects that consume the dead
key_terms.معتبر: A lesson, moral admonition, something to take heed from

ai.seo_question: What did Malik ibn Dinar say when he visited the graveyard?
ai.summary: Malik ibn Dinar, the famous ascetic of Basra (d. 130 AH), recounts visiting a graveyard and reciting poetry lamenting the fate of the great and powerful. A disembodied voice answered from among the graves with verses reminding him that all have perished without a trace, that earthly creatures erode their beauty, and that the sight of death should itself be a lesson for the living. This narration was a common feature in the literary assemblies (amali) of Shia scholars, used to encourage renunciation of worldly attachment and reflection on mortality.
word_analysis: and I called out to them

en.mulla-asgharali-m-m-jaffer: 8. He said: Abul Hasan ‘Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Katib informed me from Abu ‘Ali Muhammad ibn Hammam al-Iskafi, who reported from Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Tirmidhi, who reported from Ubaidullah ibn Umar al-Qawariri, who reported from Ja’far ibn Sulaiman al-Dhubaee’ who said: Once, I came to a deserted graveyard and I heard Malik ibn Dinar say that:

"I have come to the graves and exclaimed, Where are great ones, and where are those who were considered lowly; And where are those who were promptly answered when they summoned, And where is the mighty one, proud of his might? And where is the one conceited about his authority, And where is the powerful one, who wielded his prowess?"

He said: A voice answered me, though I would see no face; "They vied each other for destruction, and there is no sign, they all died, and (with them) the news (about them) died. The earthly insects and worms come and go, and destroy the beauty of those faces, O, he who asks about the people bygone, Is there no lesson for you in what you see?
And may Allah bless our master Muhammad and his immaculate progeny
